anchor_scope: sanity-stack input timeout_s (default 60, retry 5 s), its lock_timeout result, dev-sanity's handling, the stack bead lease
anchor_statement: sanity-stack must take a timeout for the stack bead claim, and on expiry must return the holder's identity, claim time and active task; dev-sanity must then keep the sanity task active, ask the holder once, continue other sanity work and retry; neither may refuse the task, fail the dev or escalate to a person.

cases.text: sanity-stack returns lock_timeout {holder: team-lead, since: ..., task: ...} after 60 s; dev-sanity notes STACK.LOCK_WAIT, messages team-lead once, runs its other sanity checks, retries.
dev-sanity closes the sanity task refused because the lock was busy, or sends the dev a FAIL, or sends the user a message asking who holds the lock.

sanity-stack accepts a timeout for the stack bead claim; if the claim is not obtained in time it returns lock_timeout with the holder, the claim time and the holder's active task. dev-sanity then keeps the sanity task active, messages the holder once, carries on with its other sanity work and retries; nobody refuses the task, fails the dev or asks a person.

cases.rationale: In-scope claim, silent about the timeout path.
cases.text: sanity-stack claims the stack bead before appending a layer and releases it afterwards.
sanity-stack waits on the stack bead claim with no time limit until the bead is free.

cases.rationale: Escalation to a person is ruled out.
cases.text: On lock_timeout dev-sanity messages Rand to ask who holds the stack lock.
Every time atm-bd prints for a person is rendered in 24-hour local time.
